title: Circular Measure Module 2 Lesson 1: Chords, Circular Segments & Compound Geometry custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, values and combinations are original; mapped Cambridge evidence informs scope and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A chord $AB$ in a circle of radius $12\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle of $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$ at the centre. Find the exact length of the chord $AB$.
A triangle $OAB$ is formed by two radii $OA = OB = 8\text{ cm}$ of a circle and chord $AB$, where angle $AOB = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$. Find the exact area of triangle $OAB$.
A circle has radius $10\text{ cm}$. A chord subtends an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$ at the centre. Find the exact area of the minor segment enclosed by the chord and the arc.
A chord in a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$ at the centre. Find the exact perimeter of the minor segment.

In a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$, two radii $OA$ and $OB$ contain an acute angle $\theta\text{ radians}$. The area of triangle $OAB$ is $9\text{ cm}^2$. Find the exact value of $\theta$ in terms of $\pi$.
A circle of radius $4\text{ cm}$ has a minor segment of area $(4\pi - 8)\text{ cm}^2$. Find the exact area of the corresponding major segment.
A circle has radius $10\text{ cm}$. Chord $AB$ subtends $\pi/3\text{ radians}$ at the centre. Find $AB$ exactly.
